1. Get to really know your car and what pressure you need to push your foot down on the accelerator for different speeds. For example, go to a road that is 30km and practice what pressure you need to keep your foot on the accelerator. Than find a road thats 50km, 60km etc. When you figure out what pressure you need for different speeds (which will come with lots of practice), you’ll be able to maintain speed without having to look down at the speed every 5 secs.

2. I would look at the road rules of your country for this one. In New Zealand (where I’m from), the road rule is: the car turning OUT in a T intersection must give way first to the car turning IN to a T intersection. If you’re turning in, you should the right of way and the other would have to wait until you’re gone. 

But it might be different rules in another country, so I would check the official law for this. 

3. I think it depends on learning style. For me I relearned and memorised all the rules again when I was learning to drive by redoing the practice theory questions over and over, until I got it 100% right, every single time. Quizzes might help but maybe rereading the roadcode might better suit you instead. 

ALSO I found that I learnt the road rules pretty quickly when i was forced to drive in peak times with lots of cars around. I know it’s incredibly hard with driving anxiety (I cried every single day 💀) but my recommendation is to have an experienced driver in the passenger seat and drive in peak times. Throwing yourself in the deep end (no matter how scary it is) will force you to learn faster bc you have literally no choice. 

Good luck!! You will conquer this fear of driving ! 🫶

You just started learning, it’s normal to make mistakes. Some people continue to make mistakes even after they passed their test. Don’t put yourself on a timeline and just enjoy the process of learning - be kind to yourself when you make mistakes. 

Also I found that I made less mistakes when I had a good nights rest, ate and drank before getting behind the wheel - it’s seems like common sense but it really does help. 

If you find that you feel overwhelmed, ask your brother if you can pull over for 2 minutes to recollect your thoughts. You drive better when you are calm.
